title: Systems and automation in Scottsdale, AZ | Creosote Labs
meta_description: Creosote Labs consolidates spreadsheets and disconnected tools into one system for Scottsdale businesses and automates repetitive work. Review is $3,000.
intro: Many Scottsdale businesses in hospitality, healthcare, real estate, and financial services run on a mix of a core platform and a set of spreadsheets that grew up around it. A property management company might keep leases in AppFolio and vendor work orders in Excel; a medical practice might schedule in its EHR and track referrals in Google Sheets; a tour operator might take bookings online and manage guides and vehicles on a whiteboard. The gaps between those tools are where data gets re-entered and follow-up gets missed.

Creosote Labs works with Scottsdale businesses to replace that mix with one system of record. We spend a day on site documenting the current process, then deliver a written assessment with a quote for each recommendation. From there we consolidate the spreadsheets, build the internal tools the business needs for scheduling, quoting, tracking, and reporting, and automate data entry, follow-up, and document generation. Every system is documented and handed over to staff so it can be run without us.
projects: A vendor work order tracker for a property management company that replaces an Excel log and syncs unit and owner data from AppFolio.
A trip roster and guide scheduling tool for a tour operator that pulls confirmed bookings into one calendar and generates the day's manifest.
A referral tracking system for a specialty medical practice that logs incoming referrals, assigns follow-up, and reports turnaround time.
An automated proposal generator for a landscaping company that builds an estimate and contract from a site visit form and pushes the job to QuickBooks.
A client onboarding workflow for a financial advisory practice that collects documents, populates the CRM, and produces the account opening packet.

faqs.q: Do we have to replace the software we already use?
faqs.a: Not usually, since most projects keep the core platform, such as AppFolio, QuickBooks, or a practice management system, and replace the spreadsheets and manual steps around it. The operations review identifies which pieces are worth keeping.
Implementation is quoted from the one-day operations review, which is $3,000 and credited toward work that begins within 90 days. Pricing is fixed scope, with no hourly billing.

faqs.q: Who maintains the system after it is built?
faqs.a: Staff do. Every system is delivered with written documentation and handed over to the people who will run it, and it runs on tools the business controls.
